archetype.name: Dual-Threat (pass-first, legs as release valve)
archetype.definition: A quarterback whose value has always come from pairing downfield accuracy with scrambles and designed runs, though in 2026 the running faded and the passing carried the load unevenly before injury ended his season.

report.headline: Season over after five uneven starts: downfield passing worked, everything underneath didn't.
report.take:
The news comes first. Hurts is on Injured Reserve with a calf injury, and the October 19 report says new imaging found several blood clots in his lungs. He is expected to be kept out of football activities for months and to miss the rest of the season, with an estimated return date of February 15, 2027. Tanner McKee started Week 6, and Hurts now sits fourth on the depth chart. Whatever this card says about his play, he will not add to these numbers this year.

What he leaves behind is a split season. Throws of 10 or more air yards were excellent: +0.878 EPA per attempt, a CPOE of +8.7, and six of his eight touchdowns. Throws under 10 yards were bad: -0.352 per attempt, a CPOE of -7.1, and an EPA total that cancels almost all of the downfield gains. Throws behind the line were the worst of all, with screens and swings succeeding just 9.1% of the time. His bad-throw rate of 21.4% ranked last among 37 charted passers, up 7.1 points from last season. His career rates sat around 12.5% to 14.5% from 2021 through 2025, and his CPOE ran positive every year from 2021 on, peaking at +7.5 in 2024. That makes the short-game accuracy collapse look like a change, not who he is.

The decline also got worse as the weeks went on. Over Weeks 3 through 5 the Eagles went 0-3. He averaged -0.199 EPA per dropback with a CPOE of -9.9, and Week 4 against the Rams bottomed out at 12-of-27 for 93 yards with a 36% bad-throw rate. The running game that used to make him dangerous shrank too: designed runs averaged 1.11 yards and were stuffed 55.6% of the time. Scrambles still paid, at +0.33 EPA each. His listed injury is a calf, but the dossier can't say whether it was limiting him before it was diagnosed, so treat that link as an open question.

The context around him was poor as well. Philadelphia ranks 28th in offensive EPA and 31st in success rate. He was pressured on 28.7% of dropbacks, among the heaviest rates in the league, and he worked behind a line now missing Lane Johnson and Landon Dickerson. One receiver produced: Dontayvion Wicks added +0.735 EPA per target, while DeVonta Smith, on the same 27 targets, barely broke even. This was a quarterback doing his damage in chunks inside a broken short game, and that wasn't working well enough to win.

strengths.title: Intermediate and deep accuracy held up
strengths.body: On throws of 10 or more air yards he completed passes well above expectation and generated almost all of his positive value, including six touchdowns. That matches his career profile as an efficient downfield passer, so it was real skill rather than a hot streak. He just couldn't lean on it often enough.

strengths.title: Red-zone finishing and ball security
strengths.body: He threw five touchdowns on 14 red-zone attempts with a strong CPOE there, and he lost no fumbles. His touchdown rate ran above league average even as everything else sagged. On a sample this small the red-zone number would likely have cooled.

strengths.title: Scrambles still created value
strengths.body: Even with the designed run game stuffed, his off-script scrambles averaged +0.33 EPA and moved the chains five times. The legs were still worth something as an escape hatch, just not as a called weapon.

concerns.title: Season-ending blood clots
concerns.body: New imaging revealed several blood clots in his lungs, and he is expected to miss the rest of the season. This is a medical issue first. His 2027 outlook depends on recovery, not on football form.

concerns.title: Short-game accuracy collapse
concerns.body: Throws under 10 yards and behind the line drained value at a rate unlike anything in his career. His bad-throw rate ranked dead last among charted passers. Against a career of positive CPOE, this looks like a cause-driven change, whether health, protection or something else, rather than his baseline.

concerns.title: Designed run game was dead
concerns.body: Called runs averaged barely a yard and were stuffed more than half the time. That removed a pillar of the offense that ranked him top-ten in rushing for most of his career. Some of this traces to the line and the team rushing EPA ranking 27th, not just to him.

trend.note: He opened with two wins and positive EPA, including a +15.9 CPOE game at Tennessee. Then came three straight losses at -0.199 EPA per dropback and a -9.9 CPOE, the worst stretch before the injury ended his season.

nextGame.headline: Hurts is out; McKee gets Dallas's leaky pass defense
nextGame.body:
Hurts will not play Week 7. He is on IR and expected to miss the season, and Tanner McKee started in his place in Week 6. That is a shame for his profile, because Dallas ranks last in pass EPA allowed. It also ranks 31st both on short throws, exactly where Hurts was failing, and in explosive pass rate. Opponents' lead receivers have beaten their usual output against this defense.

The availability that matters belongs to McKee now. He plays without right tackle Lane Johnson (out) and guard Landon Dickerson (IR), with Saquon Barkley out and the top tight-end depth on IR. Dallas is missing cornerback Cobie Durant, and linebacker Dee Winters is doubtful. The Book has Philadelphia as 4.5-point home underdogs against a Dallas offense ranked sixth in EPA, which points to a game where the Eagles have to throw.

keyMatchups.title: Dallas's porous short-pass defense
keyMatchups.body: Dallas allows the second-worst EPA on short throws and the worst pass EPA overall. That is the area where Hurts's season fell apart, and it is now McKee's opportunity.

keyMatchups.title: Patched line versus Dallas rush
keyMatchups.body: Dallas rarely gets home, ranking 28th in sack rate. That gives a line missing two 100%-snap starters a chance to hold up.

nextGame.watch: Whether McKee can make the underneath game function against the league's worst pass defense. That would say how much of Hurts's short-game slump belonged to the offense and how much to him.

restOfSeason.body:
There is no rest of season for Hurts. He is expected to miss the remaining games with blood clots in his lungs, so the projected ranges below are zero. For the longer view, his downfield accuracy and scrambling held up, while the short-game collapse and bad-throw spike break from five years of positive CPOE. The 2026 sample is five games of compromised play, protection and health, not a new baseline.

Any return question belongs to 2027 and to doctors, not to this stat line. Red-zone efficiency on 14 attempts and the 0-3 slide should both be read as small-sample noise around a player whose career norm is a top-half efficient passer with rushing value.
swingFactors: Any change to the expected season-long absence
Whether 2027 accuracy returns to his career norm

confidence.note: Season-ending status is clearly reported; the five-start performance sample itself is small.
